doc: The judgment tabs of the labeling page (Platform-infra azure-function-api/shared/atom-labeling-judgments.js HEADS), as model questions. Layer and space come from the label_heads.json head that lists the judgment. size: line = one line; pair = two lines; group = a document, table or sheet (its lines pooled); deal = the whole deal pooled. alias: the judgment asks an existing line question in other words, so its verdicts become that question's targets instead of a new head. Vocabularies must match parser-os app/core/pm_feedback.py HEAD_REGISTRY where it declares candidates (tests/test_c3_judgments.py checks).

conflict.subject: How these two lines relate
conflict.question: Two lines the parser thought might disagree. Do they really conflict?

answers.contradicts: They state incompatible facts about the same thing; at most one can hold.
answers.supports: They agree; one confirms or restates the other.
answers.excludes: One carves the other out of scope: a stated exception or exclusion.
answers.unrelated: They are about different things; no conflict and no support.

site.subject: One place or two
site.question: Two site names from the deal. Are they the same physical place?

answers.same_site: The same physical place under two names or spellings.

site_role.subject: Where the work happens
site_role.question: A place the deal names. Does work happen there? A site later removed from the job still answers as it was planned.

answers.job_site: Technicians go there to do the work, now or as planned before a removal.
answers.vendor_or_billing_address: No work happens there: a head office, billing or remit-to address, a vendor's or partner's office, a ship-from warehouse.

geo_mention.subject: Named place
geo_mention.question: A place named in the line. Is it a work site or only a mention?

answers.job_site: The work happens at this place.
answers.mention_only: The place is mentioned (a head office, a city in a signature, a comparison) but no work happens there.

facility.subject: Site label
facility.question: How should this address be named as a site?

answers.city_office: Name it by its city; the text gives no better name.
answers.keep_facility: Keep the facility name the text gives (a building, campus or store).
answers.keep_name: Keep the name exactly as written.

gap.subject: Worth asking
gap.question: A question the parser would ask the customer about this line. Would a person actually ask it?

answers.valid: A real open question worth asking the customer.
answers.invalid: Not worth asking: already answered, a duplicate, or the wrong question for this job.

question_answered.subject: Question answered
question_answered.question: An open question in the deal. Has a later line already answered it?

answers.open: Still open; nothing in the deal answers it.

task_tier.subject: Line or step
task_tier.question: A task line. Is it priced as a line of its own on the quote, or is it a step inside a priced line? Decide by the deal's priced lines, not by the wording or the indentation.

answers.parent: A price attaches to this task by itself.
answers.child: No price of its own: a step inside a priced line, or a seller step outside the quote.

image.subject: Image kind
image.question: A picture in a document. What kind of picture is it?

answers.table_image: A table captured as an image.
answers.label: A product or equipment label.

facet.subject: Brief section
facet.question: Which section of a project brief does this line belong in?

answers.WORK: What is done: the work itself.
answers.SITE: Where: the places and their conditions.

doc_kind.subject: What kind of document it is
doc_kind.question: A document in the deal. What kind of paper is it, judged by what it is for: who makes it, for whom, and at what stage of the deal it is written? The same words can sit in a customer's request form and in the provider's own statement of work; the kind is what the document is for, not its file type or how its lines are laid out.

answers.email: A message between the people on the deal: asks, answers, updates and forwarded files, written at any stage by any side.
answers.call_transcript: The words spoken on a call or meeting, captured as they were said; any side, any stage.
answers.meeting_recap: A summary of a call or meeting written afterwards (by a person or a meeting tool), with its decisions and next steps.
answers.crm_note: A short note a salesperson logs about the deal in their own system: who called, what was said, what is next.
answers.request_form: A form the customer or partner fills in to ask for the work before any price: job details, sites, dates, contacts.
answers.rfp: The customer's or partner's formal request for proposals or quotes, with the scope and terms bidders must answer, issued before any price.
answers.site_list: The customer's or partner's list of the places where the work happens, with their addresses and per-site facts.
answers.site_survey_report: The findings of a walk of the site before the work is priced or planned: measurements, photos, readings, what is there.
answers.site_checklist: A checklist the crew fills in at a site during or after the work: steps done, serials, issues found.
answers.equipment_list: A list of the equipment or materials for the job: models, quantities, which site each goes to.
answers.vendor_quote_bom: A supplier's priced quote or bill of materials for equipment, sent to whoever buys the hardware.
answers.vendor_datasheet: A manufacturer's product sheet: specifications of one model, the same for every job.
answers.drawing: A floor plan, elevation, design or diagram of where things go, from the customer, the designer or the installer.
answers.customer_layout_deck: The customer's own slide deck or layout pack describing its sites, standards or programme.
answers.install_guide: Step-by-step instructions for installing or setting up equipment, from the manufacturer or the customer.
answers.process_document: The customer's or partner's standing procedure, policy or runbook: how its jobs are run, the same across jobs.
answers.purchase_order: The buyer's order for the work at an agreed price, issued after the quote is accepted.
answers.invoice: A bill for work done or equipment supplied, sent after the work or a milestone.
answers.tax_form_w9: A tax form a party fills in to be set up as a vendor; paperwork, not the job.
answers.credit_application: A form to open credit or a vendor account; paperwork, not the job.
answers.nda: A confidentiality agreement between the parties, signed before details are shared.
answers.partner_sow: A statement of work written by the partner or reseller on its own paper, which the provider is asked to work under.
answers.sow_template: A blank or standard statement-of-work form, before it is written for this job.
answers.sow_draft: The provider's own statement of work for this job, before it is signed: what the provider proposes to do, at the quote stage.
answers.sow_signed: The provider's statement of work as signed by the parties: what was agreed, after the sale.
answers.change_request: A request or order to change the agreed scope, price or schedule after the work is sold.
answers.quote: The provider's own price for the job as sent to the buyer.
answers.deal_kit: The provider's own internal costing sheet for the job: its hours, rates, costs and margins, worked out before the quote and never sent as is.
answers.estimating_calc: The provider's own calculator or sheet that works out quantities, hours or cost for the price.
answers.pricing_workbook: A workbook of prices or rates (a rate card or price list) used to build a quote, the provider's or a partner's.
answers.photo: A picture: of a site, of equipment, or a screenshot.
answers.other: A document of a kind none of the others names.

document_job.subject: Document belongs to this job
document_job.question: A document in the deal. Is it about this job, or another job for the same customer?

answers.other_job: About another job; it should not shape this one.

rule.subject: Parser rule call
rule.question: A line the parser ran one of its meaning rules on; the rule is named with the line. Should that rule fire on this line? Decide by what the line means and does in its document (a heading, a label, a lead-in, an answer, an item of a list), not by its wording, its capitals or its length.

answers.should_fire: The line is what the rule looks for, so the rule should fire on it.
answers.should_not_fire: The line is not what the rule looks for, so the rule should stay quiet on it.

rules.image_field_label: Is the line a short field label whose value is the picture right below it (Signature, Floor Plan, Rack Elevation, Wiring Diagram, Before and After), so the picture is captioned by it rather than by a photo request further up the page? A name, a yes or no answer, a question or a numbered section is not one.
rules.docx_subsection_blocks_lift: Is the line a sub-heading that goes against a preamble saying what the provider will do, such as Out of Scope, Exclusions, Customer Responsibilities or Items provided by others, so the preamble must not carry onto the bullets under it? A heading of the provider's own work or a list of the customer's places is not one.
rules.list_lead_in: Does the line announce a list that follows it (the vendor will perform the following services, Deliverables:, the following are out of scope:), whatever the list is about? A sentence that states its own fact with nothing listed under it is not one.
rules.document_title_line: Does the line read as the title of a document or a section (a project name, Statement of Work, Project Overview), rather than something that belongs with the document's details: a date, page furniture, an id, a clock time or a bare value?
rules.qa_answer_block: Is the line the answer to the question just above it in a numbered question-and-answer or RFI list, so the two fold into one fact? A line of a scope of work, a bullet of a list or a new question is not one.
rules.meeting_section_header: Is the line a section header of meeting notes (Action Items, Key Decisions, Attendees, Next Steps, Agenda) that heads the lines under it? A sentence that mentions those words, a speaker's line or a fact from the meeting is not one.
rules.list_item_under_label: Is the line one of the items listed under the label above it, a fact the list enumerates, rather than prose that has moved on and ends the list (a closing remark, a pleasantry, a question back)? Length does not decide it.
rules.hours_effort_metric_label: Does the column header name a labor effort or hours measure (Lead Tech Hrs, PM Hrs, Man-Days, Crew Hours, Engineering Effort) that an hours estimate is checked against? A money, count or date column is not one.
rules.form_field_report_page: Does the page read as a form or field report (questions, labelled fields, photo requests, signatures) rather than flowing prose, a contract clause or a rate card or bill of materials, so its lines are worth regrouping as form fields?
rules.photo_request_instruction: Is the line an instruction to take or upload a photo (Upload 4 photos of the unit installed, Take a photo of the rack), the request a picture below it answers? A line that only mentions a photo is not one.
rules.section_title: Is the heading a generic section of a document (Introduction, General Conditions, Scope of Work) rather than the real title of the document or the deal, such as a company or project name?
rules.xlsx_money_header: Does the spreadsheet column header name an amount of money (Unit Price, Sell Price, Extended Price, Burdened Rate, MSRP)? A quantity, hours, a part number or a description column is not one.
rules.pl_margin_pct_label: Is the line the label of a margin percentage in a profit and loss sheet (Margin % on Total Deal, Margin % on Labor)? A money amount, a cost line or a markup that is not a margin percentage is not one.
rules.scope_work_item_heading: Does the short heading name a work activity of the scope (Unit Wiring, Media Panel Installation, Common Area buildout), rather than a stray capitalized line such as a place name, a person or a date label?

roster.subject: Site list
roster.question: A table in the deal. Is it a list of the job's sites?

answers.site_roster: A list of the places where the work happens.

sheet.subject: Sheet role
sheet.question: A sheet of a workbook. What is it for?

answers.reference: Background to look things up in.
answers.instructions: How to fill in or use the workbook.

billing_type.subject: How the job is billed
billing_type.question: How does the signed or latest scope of work bill this job?

answers.fixed: One price for the stated scope, whatever the hours turn out to be.
answers.t_and_m: Hours, days or units times a rate, so every total is an estimate; a per-day rate times sites and days is still time and materials.
answers.milestone: Payments tied to stages of the work: a deposit, a mid-point and a completion payment.
answers.per_site: A fixed price per site, times the number of sites.

materials_scope.subject: Consumables
materials_scope.question: Does the job include consumables (fasteners, cable ties, patch cords)?

expenses_scope.subject: Expenses
expenses_scope.question: Are expenses (shipping, per diem, freight) billed on this job?

travel_scope.subject: Travel
travel_scope.question: Is travel (mileage, airfare, hotel, drive time) billed on this job?

tier.subject: Project tier
tier.question: Which of the company's project tiers is this job?

services.subject: Services the job includes
services.question: The deal as a whole. Which kinds of field service does the job include, all of them, not only the main one? Decide from what the customer and partner ask for and what the scope of work carries: a camera install that also runs the camera cable is security_camera and low_voltage_cabling; a side task that is part of another service (mounting a bracket for a display) is not a service of its own.

answers.audio_visual: Installing displays, projectors, video-conferencing systems, kiosks or speakers and making them work; any cabling is only there to serve them.
answers.low_voltage_cabling: Running, terminating, labelling and testing data or voice cable (copper or fibre), with the racks, cabinets, patch panels and backboards that hold it.
answers.wireless: Wireless networks: surveying, installing or moving access points and the runs that feed them.
answers.staff_augmentation: Technicians supplied by the day or the hour for recurring or on-call on-site support under the customer's direction, not a defined install.
answers.security_camera: Installing and connecting security cameras, with their mounts, power and runs.
answers.camera_vms_operations: Operating or maintaining a video system after the install: configuration, health checks, footage requests.
answers.security_access: Access control: card readers, door hardware, controllers and intercom entry.
answers.fire_safety: Fire alarm, detection or suppression work.
answers.paging_mass_notification: Paging, overhead speakers and mass-notification systems.
answers.das: A distributed antenna system or cellular signal boosting inside a building.
answers.electrical: Line-voltage electrical work: circuits, outlets, panels.
answers.telecom: Telephony and carrier work: phone systems, handsets, voice migrations, circuits and demarcation points.
answers.network_maintenance: Ongoing upkeep of an existing network: switch and router changes, troubleshooting, scheduled maintenance.
answers.building_management_systems: Building controls: HVAC, lighting or sensor controllers and their networks.
answers.datacenter: Work inside a data centre: build-outs, moves, structured power and cooling for computer rooms.
answers.rack_and_stack: Mounting servers and network gear in racks and cabling them, with no wider install.
answers.hardware: Supplying equipment is the main thing sold; labour is incidental.
answers.imac: Install, move, add or change of end-user and point-of-sale devices: computers, Chromebooks, registers, printers, peripherals, including removing and packing old ones.
answers.itad: Retiring IT assets: decommission, data wipe, recycling or resale.
answers.data_migration: Moving data or systems from one platform to another.
answers.msp: A standing managed-services contract: remote monitoring and support for a monthly fee.
answers.alm: Asset lifecycle management: tagging, tracking and refresh logistics for a fleet of devices.
answers.audit: The deliverable is a survey, inventory or assessment of what is on site, not an install.
answers.professional_services: Design, consulting or project management with no field install.
answers.other: A field service none of the others names.

end_customer.subject: Who the work is for
end_customer.question: The deal as a whole; the card's query asks it. Is the company the work is ultimately for named, and where? When a reseller or partner buys the work, the end customer is the company at whose sites it happens; when the buyer is that company, the buyer is the end customer. The card links to the line that names it.

answers.named: A line names the company the work is ultimately for; the card links to it.
answers.not_named: No line names the company the work is for: only the buyer, a brand or a site is given, so it has to be asked.

delivery_model.subject: What shape the delivery takes
delivery_model.question: The deal as a whole. What does the field work mainly consist of: building something out, configuring what is already in place, or surveying and designing before anything is built? Decide from what is asked and what the scope carries, not from the equipment brand.

answers.install_buildout: Equipment or cable is put in place: mounting, running, terminating, racking, with any configuration that comes with it.
answers.config_only: Everything is already physically installed; the work is configuration, programming or bring-up only.
answers.survey_design: The work is a survey, assessment or design before any build: walks, measurements, RF readings, inventories, drawings.
answers.service_support: Ongoing or on-call hands on site: break-fix, smart hands, maintenance visits, with no defined build.

exclusion_set.subject: A standard exclusion for this job
exclusion_set.question: The deal as a whole; the card's query names one exclusion jobs of this trade commonly carry (electrical work, lift rental, core drilling, wall repair, network configuration, licensing, transport, disposal, data destruction, permits, equipment supply). Does this job leave it out, take it on, or not touch it at all?

answers.excluded: The job leaves it out: it is the customer's or someone else's, or not done at all, and the scope of work says so or the customer says so.
answers.included: The job takes it on: the provider does or supplies it as part of the work.
answers.not_applicable: The job's work never comes near it, so there is nothing to include or exclude.

sow_slot.subject: Where the SOW slot's content comes from
sow_slot.question: One slot of one section of the statement of work this job will need; the card's query names the section and the kind of fact the slot holds (a start date, a site contact, the site list, a price, the work steps). Before the SOW is written, where will that slot's content come from? Judge from what the customer and partner have said so far, not from how any document is laid out.

answers.template: The section's standard wording covers it; no fact of this job is needed.
answers.filled: A line the customer or partner wrote before the SOW states the fact the slot needs; the card links to that line.
answers.house_default: The provider fills it from its own standing values (its own contact, document version, standard rates, uplifts or payment terms), not from anything the customer said.
answers.missing_chase: The slot needs a fact of this job that no earlier line states, so someone has to ask for it before the SOW can be finished.

not_trained.type: The atom card's type picker already teaches it.
not_trained.norm: The answer is free text; a later PR can give it to the teacher.
not_trained.commercial: Purtera's Deal Kit shape (billing, PM/PC hours, travel days): company layer (conduct.constants), never the base. The answer is free text.
not_trained.term: The answer is key=value (app.core.commercial_term_read); a later PR can give it to the teacher.
not_trained.terminology: The answer is free text; a later PR can give it to the teacher.
not_trained.hours: Task hours: a later PR can map it onto the labor hours number.
